description: Four incidental findings from TKT-92's adversarial ai-review (gpt-5.6-sol@claudex), real but out of scope for the taxonomy/bounding PR (#63): (1) attempt lag is measured at goroutine spawn, not at attempt start — under scheduler pressure CeilingInconclusive can accept a rate that was not delivered on schedule; (2) loadClient follows redirects and forwards X-Internal-Token on same-host redirects — pin CheckRedirect to fail closed; (3) every hold 409 counts as an expected capacity rejection — archived/closed-slot/idempotency 409s are indistinguishable from sellout; consider discriminating on the error body; (4) finalize/confirm validate status only — an empty/malformed 200 body counts as KindOK despite the taxonomy classifying malformed success bodies as server errors. Natural home: whichever of TKT-31/TKT-37 next touches the harness.

# TKT-93 — Load-harness measurement fidelity follow-ups: execution plan

Four measurement-fidelity fixes to the on-sale load harness. No product-path changes. Taxonomy reminder that governs every classification choice below (from TKT-92 comments in `loadtest.go:19-29` and `onsale_load_test.go:91-95`): **client-error is never a server verdict** (it makes a run inconclusive); **a delivered forbidden status decides alone**; **unrecognized/malformed success bodies are server-error**. A redirect response is a delivered forbidden status, not a transport failure.

## 1. Test seam — where each finding bites

- `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest_test.go` runs untagged (`package loadtest`, internal white-box) under `make test-go`; `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` is `//go:build smoke` and needs the compose stack. `make check` runs both.
- **Finding 1 (lag at spawn, not start)** — unit-testable where it lives. `RunStage` takes `AttemptFunc`, so the seam already exists: an attempt func that blocks on a gate channel until the scheduler has spawned all workers forces spawn/start divergence deterministically. No refactor needed; keep the mutex bookkeeping (see §5).
- **Finding 2 (redirect following)** — the policy is 3 lines on `loadClient`, but *verifying* it needs an HTTP round-trip. Make it unit-testable by moving the client construction into `smoke/internal/loadtest`: `func NewClient() *http.Client` (transport bounds + timeout + pinned `CheckRedirect`). `onsale_load_test.go` then does `var loadClient = loadtest.NewClient()`. A unit test pins the policy against `httptest.NewServer` — stdlib, already imported transitively, no new dependency. This is the only helper move; `timedPost` itself stays in the smoke package.
- **Finding 3 (409 discrimination)** — extract a pure function into the loadtest package: `func ClassifyHold409(body []byte) string` (returns `KindRejected` or `KindServerError`). `checkoutAttempt` calls it instead of unconditionally returning `KindRejected`. Table-driven unit tests, no stack.
- **Finding 4 (finalize/confirm body validation)** — extract the pure predicate: `func ValidTransitionBody(body []byte, wantStatus string) bool`. `checkoutAttempt`'s step loop calls it after a clean 200. Table-driven unit tests, no stack.
- Findings 3 and 4 keep their *integration* verification in the smoke suite implicitly: the gate profile exercises real finalize/confirm bodies and a real 409 sellout tail, so a false positive in either predicate fails the gate loudly.

## 2. DoD — mapped to COS

| COS | Done when |
|---|---|
| COS1 | `RunStage` captures lag at attempt start (first line of the worker goroutine), not at spawn. New unit test `TestLagMeasuredAtAttemptStart` demonstrates a scheduler-delayed spawn produces a lag sample > the spawn-time value (red before the fix: samples stay ~0). |
| COS2 | `loadClient` (via `loadtest.NewClient`) pins `CheckRedirect` → `http.ErrUseLastResponse`. Unit test: a POST to an `httptest` 302 handler returns the 302 response itself — no hop, target handler never hit. In `checkoutAttempt`, a 3xx on any step classifies `KindServerError` via the existing "forbidden status decides alone" rule (it is not 409/201/200). No code path can re-issue the request, so `X-Internal-Token` cannot be re-sent by the transport; the test asserts the redirect target was never called. |
| COS3 | `checkoutAttempt` on hold 409 calls `ClassifyHold409`: body carrying `"code":"slot_archived"` or `"code":"slot_closed"` → `KindServerError`; bare `{"error":…}` (the `ErrUnavailable`/`ErrConflict`/`ErrIdempotency` shape) → `KindRejected`; any other shape (unparseable, foreign `code` value, missing `error`) → `KindServerError`. Unit table test covers all four rows. |
| COS4 | After a clean-200 finalize/confirm, `ValidTransitionBody` requires parseable JSON whose `status` equals the step's target (`finalizing` / `confirmed`). Empty, unparseable, wrong-status, or missing-status body → `KindServerError` with the body snippet in `Note`, matching the `KindServerError` doc ("malformed body on a success status"). Unit table test; gate profile's real lifecycle proves no false positive on the healthy path. |
| COS5 | `make check` green (unit package + smoke gate profile). No change to `Accounting` queries, `HistoryStats` collection, stage profile shapes, or the `3×lifecycle` claim_history pin. |

## 3. Files and shape of each change

**`smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go`** (3 small additions, one 2-line move):
- `RunStage`: delete `lag := time.Since(scheduled)` at `loadtest.go:99`; inside the worker goroutine, first statement: `lag := time.Since(scheduled)` (closure captures `scheduled`). The `res.Lag` append stays under `mu` — only the capture point moves. Comment update: "scheduled-start lag measured at attempt start (TKT-93), so scheduler backpressure shows up in the sample."
- Add `NewClient() *http.Client` — the transport bounds (`MaxIdleConns`/`MaxIdleConnsPerHost` 1024, `MaxConnsPerHost` from a `MaxConnsPerHost` const moved here too), 15s timeout, and `CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }`. Comment: fail-closed redirect policy — a redirect is a delivered forbidden status the attempt classifies, never a followed hop; the internal token is never re-sent (TKT-93, ADR-028 posture).
- Add `ClassifyHold409(body []byte) string` — parses `{"error":…,"code":…}`; known non-capacity codes (`slot_archived`, `slot_closed`) → `KindServerError`; well-formed body with no `code` → `KindRejected` (that is exactly the sellout/conflict/idempotency shape `problem()` emits); anything else → `KindServerError`. Comment ties this to ADR-028's fail-closed drift posture and names the known-code list as derived from `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go problem()` (with the note that a fixture built from the code under test cannot fail — the strings are pinned as literals, not imported).
- Add `ValidTransitionBody(body []byte, wantStatus string) bool` — parse JSON, require `status == wantStatus`. Checks only the field the harness depends on (identity was established by the hold step); this is malformed-body detection, not schema validation.

**`smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest_test.go`** — new tests (TDD order in §4), all untagged, all stdlib.

**`smoke/onsale_load_test.go`**:
- Replace the literal `loadClient` var with `var loadClient = loadtest.NewClient()`; move `maxClientConnsPerHost` into the loadtest package (exported) and keep the `report.ClientMaxConnsPerHost` line referencing it.
- Hold 409 branch (`onsale_load_test.go:99`): `return loadtest.Outcome{Kind: loadtest.ClassifyHold409(body), Note: ...}` — note carries the body snippet when server-error.
- Step loop: after the `code != http.StatusOK` / `err != nil` cases, add `case !loadtest.ValidTransitionBody(rbody, stepTarget):` → `KindServerError`. The `step` struct gains a `target` field (`"finalizing"`, `"confirmed"`).

No other files. No new dependencies (`httptest` is stdlib). No changes to `poolAccounting`, `historyInsertStats`, or any stage/profile constant.

## 4. Test plan — TDD order

1. **Finding 1 — `TestLagMeasuredAtAttemptStart`** (write first, observe red): stage rate 100/s × 50ms (5 arrivals), `maxInFlight` 8, attempt func closes over a `gate chan struct{}` and blocks on `<-gate`. Main test goroutine sleeps ~150ms after `RunStage` returns... no — `RunStage` waits on `wg`, so instead: run `RunStage` in a goroutine, sleep 150ms, close `gate`, collect result. Assert `Percentile(res.Lag, 99) >= 100ms`. Red today because lag is captured at spawn (≈ sub-ms); green after the capture moves into the worker.
2. **Finding 3 — `TestClassifyHold409`** (red): table — `{"error":"…","code":"slot_archived"}` → server-error; `slot_closed` → server-error; `{"error":"sold out"}` → rejected; `{"error":"…","code":"something_new"}` → server-error; `not json` → server-error; `{}` → server-error. Then implement.
3. **Finding 4 — `TestValidTransitionBody`** (red): valid `{"hold_id":"…","status":"finalizing"}` for target `finalizing` → true; `{"status":"held"}` → false; `{}` → false; empty → false; unparseable → false. Then implement.
4. **Finding 2 — `TestNewClientNeverFollowsRedirects`** (red): `httptest.NewServer` with a `/redirect` handler returning 302 → `/target` (target handler sets a hit flag). POST via `loadtest.NewClient()`; assert returned status is 302, `err == nil`, target never hit, and the delivered request to `/target` count is zero (hence no header re-send possible). Then implement.
5. Wire findings 2–4 into `checkoutAttempt` (the smoke-package call-site edits — compile-gated by `go vet -tags smoke`; no new smoke-only unit test needed since the pure predicates are already covered and the gate profile is the integration check).
6. Run `make check`. Smoke gate profile green confirms COS5 and exercises findings 3 (rejection tail: bare-`error` 409s must still classify `KindRejected` — a false server-error here fails the gate at `reject.Rejected != reject.Started`) and 4 (every real lifecycle's finalize/confirm bodies must validate).

## 5. Risks / open decisions

- **Finding 3 fail direction — decided: unrecognized 409 bodies fail to `KindServerError`, not `KindRejected`.** ADR-028's posture is that protocol drift fails closed; for the harness, "closed" means the class that *cannot be ignored*: a server-error count fails the gate run (`t.Fatalf` on any server error) and is never publishable as a healthy sellout, whereas `KindRejected` silently counts as the system working. A new `code` the harness doesn't know is exactly drift — the harness must not bless it as capacity evidence. The risk of this choice: an inventory change that adds a new 409 code breaks the gate until the harness learns it. That is the intended fail-closed cost, and the note body makes the diagnosis one log line.
- **Finding 1 capture point: inside the worker, keeping `mu`.** The alternative (a per-arrival buffered channel of lag values, or measuring in the scheduler after `wg.Add`) either adds machinery or re-introduces the spawn-time measurement. Moving one line into the goroutine is the shortest correct diff; `res.Lag` append ordering across workers is already nondeterministic and `Percentile` sorts, so nothing downstream cares. One subtlety worth a comment: lag now includes goroutine-scheduling delay after spawn — which is precisely the backpressure the p99 guard exists to catch.
- **Finding 2 surfaces 3xx as server-error via existing rules — no new kind.** A redirect from inventory/gateway is protocol-forbidden for these POSTs, and the taxonomy already says a delivered forbidden status is server evidence. `ErrUseLastResponse` (not a custom error) keeps `timedPost`'s err semantics untouched — no classification-path change, no risk of a redirect becoming an inconclusive client-error.
- **`ValidTransitionBody` scope: status field only.** Validating the full `Claim` shape duplicates the contract middleware's job (ADR-028) and buys nothing the accounting queries don't already prove; the finding asks only that empty/malformed success bodies stop counting as OK.
- **COS1 measurement fidelity vs. gate flakiness:** none expected — the gate profile doesn't assert on lag (only `CeilingInconclusive` in the full profile reads it, at a 1s limit vs. nominal ~2ms), so the more honest (larger) samples can't trip the gate.

Skipped: no redirect attempts to distinguish gateway vs inventory redirect sources, no `KindRejected` sub-counters — add when a run actually needs to split sellout causes.
